about: Nino Barraco is the son of farmers who, like many in Marsala, sold their wine in bulk to the big fortified-wine houses. With the 2004 vintage he began bottling under his own name, farming organically from the start, and he has since become one of the leading figures in Sicily’s artisanal wine movement. He now tends around twenty hectares of mostly old vines scattered along the coast north and south of Marsala, many within sight of the sea, and makes single-vineyard wines from native grapes such as Grillo, Catarratto and Zibibbo.

His sparkling wine comes from a vineyard in Contrada Corleo, near Petrosino, where some vines grow just thirty metres from the Mediterranean on red clay over shallow bedrock; winter storms can even wash seagrass into the rows. The Grillo grapes are pressed directly, the base wine rests on its lees in stainless steel until the next harvest, and the second fermentation in bottle is started with fresh Grillo must rather than added sugar and yeast. It spends more than two years on the lees and is finished pas dosé, with no added sugar at all.

Sparkling wine is an unusual turn for a Marsala grower, but it fits Barraco’s focus on Grillo, the grape that once formed the backbone of traditional Marsala. Reviewing the 2021, Eric Guido of Vinous called the wine impossible to ignore, with a long, fresh and complex finish that turns nearly salty, a fair summary of the windswept coastal vineyard it comes from. Expect a bone-dry, savoury style rather than a fruity one.
facts: Contrada Corleo, Petrosino; seaside red clay over bedrock
Metodo classico; second fermentation started with Grillo must, no added sugar or yeast
